Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

Executive Leadership & Active Management Structure

Primary SEC 20-F and Form 6-K filings confirm that PDD Holdings Inc. operates under a dual-leadership governance framework led by Co-Chairmen of the Board and Co-Chief Executive Officers Lei Chen (Co-CEO since April 2023; Co-Chairman since December 2025) and Jiazhen Zhao (Co-CEO since April 2023; Co-Chairman since December 2025). Financial operations and public earnings disclosures are directed by Jun Liu, Vice President of Finance, alongside Financial Director Jiong Li. Former founder Colin Huang holds no active operational or executive role. Under this management structure, PDD Holdings has transitioned into its second operating decade, steering core domestic platform Pinduoduo alongside cross-border e-commerce platform Temu through intense competitive dynamics and international regulatory restructuring.

Operating Performance & Macro-Regulatory Pivot

For the first quarter of 2026 (ended March 31, 2026), PDD Holdings delivered total net revenue of RMB 106.23 billion ($15.15 billion), representing an 11.0% year-over-year expansion compared to RMB 95.67 billion in Q1 2025. Top-line growth was primarily fueled by Transaction Services, which surged 20.0% year-over-year to RMB 56.30 billion, reflecting sustained marketplace order volume. GAAP operating profit reached RMB 19.60 billion ($2.79 billion), yielding a GAAP operating margin of 18.5% (+163 bps YoY). Operating cash flow for the quarter totaled RMB 16.40 billion ($2.34 billion), up 5.8% YoY, expanding PDD's massive liquid balance sheet—comprising cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments—to RMB 436.1 billion ($63.20 billion) as of March 31, 2026.

The operational landscape for Temu underwent a fundamental structural reset following the 2025/2026 complete elimination of the United States $800 de minimis customs exemption (Section 321). Previously reliant on duty-free direct-from-China small-parcel air shipments, Temu was forced to halt direct China fulfillment to US buyers to avoid tariffs exceeding 145%. Management overhauled Temu's operating model by pivoting entirely to a local bonded warehousing and domestic US seller framework (B2B2C). While local fulfillment protects consumers from direct import tariffs and improves delivery speed, it compresses unit-level gross margins, elevates local inventory holding costs, and eliminates legacy cross-border tax arbitrage. Simultaneously, PDD launched a massive RMB 100 billion multi-year supply chain upgrade initiative—supported by an initial RMB 15 billion capital injection into a dedicated Shanghai entity—to incubate first-party merchant brands and modernize agricultural logistics.

Capital Allocation Inaction vs. Super-Whale Institutional Conviction

A central paradox in PDD Holdings' fundamental profile is the extreme divergence between its capital hoarding and institutional smart-money behavior. Holding $63.20 billion in cash and liquid short-term investments, management maintains an unyielding capital allocation policy of $0 share repurchases and $0 cash dividends. Executive leadership explicitly prioritizes reinvesting all organic cash flows into merchant ecosystem subsidies, fee reductions, and supply chain infrastructure over returning capital to public equity holders. Despite this shareholder return freeze and tariff-induced stock volatility, Li Lu's Himalaya Capital Management disclosed in its Q2 2026 SEC Form 13F filing a massive +133.5% increase in its PDD stake. Himalaya acquired 6.15 million additional shares at an average price of $92.32, building a 10.76 million share position valued at $821 million. PDD now represents 22.17% of Himalaya's $3.70 billion US equity portfolio, standing as its third-largest position alongside Alphabet and Berkshire Hathaway.

(NASDAQ: PDD) operates as a global e-commerce technology group under a joint executive leadership framework directed by Co-Chairmen and Co-Chief Executive Officers Lei Chen and Jiazhen Zhao. 2. Mechanics of Monetization, Switching Costs & Pricing Power Audit

To evaluate PDD through the lens of Ben Graham and Warren Buffett, an investor must look past headline growth to examine the structural durability of how the business extracts cash from economic activity.

A. How PDD Makes Money: The Dual Engine Architecture

  • Domestic Engine (Pinduoduo): Operates an asset-light marketplace matching 900M+ price-sensitive consumers with factory-direct unbranded manufacturers and agricultural producers. PDD monetization relies on seller competition for consumer attention: merchants pay for algorithmic placement, search keyword auctions, and campaign access (Online Marketing Services) while paying a baseline transaction fee (Transaction Services).
  • Global Engine (Temu): Operates via a hybrid model transition. Under the historical Fully-Managed Model, Chinese factories shipped bulk inventory to Temu’s domestic consolidation hubs; Temu dictated end-consumer pricing, handled international air-freight, marketing, and customer service, extracting a gross spread. Following global trade regulatory shifts, Temu has aggressively scaled its Semi-Managed Model, requiring merchants to hold localized inventory in destination markets while Temu collects platform transaction fees, advertising revenues, and fulfillment service margins.

B. Customer Switching Costs: The Disincentive Asymmetry

From the end-consumer perspective, switching costs are zero. Consumers hold no structural loyalty to PDD or Temu; their purchasing decisions are governed entirely by absolute price superiority, gamified engagement (team-buying, rewards), and delivery reliability. If a competitor offers identical white-label merchandise at a lower price, consumers migrate instantly.

However, merchant switching costs are exceptionally high. Upstream factory owners and unbranded manufacturers in mainland China face severe overcapacity and razor-thin gross margins. PDD controls the primary digital distribution channel to hundreds of millions of value-seeking buyers. Because PDD's algorithm allocates order volume based strictly on lowest unit pricing and merchant operational performance, factories cannot afford to leave the platform without risking immediate factory floor shutdowns. This operational dependency allows PDD to extract sustained advertising bids and commission take rates.

C. Evidence of Pricing Power: Traffic Control vs. Merchant Extraction

PDD possesses strong pricing power over its merchants, but zero pricing power over its end-consumers:

  • Merchant Pricing Power (Strong): PDD continuously increases effective merchant take-rates by auctioning prime user feed real estate. Even as management announced a multi-year RMB 100 billion merchant support and fee-reduction initiative, transaction revenues grew 20% YoY in Q1 2026, demonstrating that merchant demand for PDD traffic remains inelastic.
  • Consumer Pricing Power (Absent): PDD cannot arbitrarily raise consumer prices. The company’s brand equity is explicitly bound to the "value-for-money" proposition. Any attempt to expand gross margins by raising consumer prices directly degrades platform volume.

4. Structural Secular Tailwinds vs. Competitive Disruption Threats

A. Structural Secular Tailwinds

  • Global Consumer Consumption Down-Trading: Persistent inflation and macroeconomic pressures across North America, Europe, and domestic China have driven a structural secular shift toward budget-conscious consumption. PDD's C2M model strips out intermediary distributor markups, positioning Pinduoduo and Temu as the primary beneficiaries of consumer down-trading.
  • Direct-from-Factory Digitization: Unbranded industrial clusters in China (and increasingly Southeast Asia) require digital export clearinghouses. Temu provides small-and-medium factories with instant access to 50+ global consumer markets without requiring in-house foreign language marketing, cross-border legal compliance, or international brand building.
  • Agile Local-to-Local Merchant Onboarding: By rapidly expanding its Semi-Managed Model, Temu is onboarding local merchants with existing regional warehouse inventory in the US and EU, reducing delivery times from 10-14 days (air parcels) to 3-5 days (domestic ground).

B. Competitive Disruption & Regulatory Threats

Regulatory Disruption: Elimination of the US $800 De Minimis Exemption
In 2025/2026, the United States executive branch and Congress enacted strict reform and ultimate elimination of the Section 321 de minimis exemption, which previously permitted duty-free entry for imported shipments valued under US $800. Coupled with European Union customs border reforms targeting low-value parcels, Temu’s historic unit economics—built on duty-free cross-border air-freight direct to individual consumers—have been permanently altered.
Operational Consequence: Temu was forced to accelerate its pivot toward local bonded warehousing, bulk sea-freight customs clearing, and localized merchant fulfillment. While this mitigates parcel-level tariff risk, it increases inventory working capital demands and fulfillment overhead, compressing Temu's long-term operating margins.
  • Capital Allocation Inaction vs. Cash Hoard Risk: PDD ended Q1 2026 with a massive balance sheet fortress of RMB 436.1 billion ($63.2 billion) in liquid cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. Despite generating robust operating cash flows (RMB 16.4 billion in Q1 2026 alone), management maintains a strict $0 buyback and $0 dividend policy. Management's commitment to spend RMB 100 billion over three years on supply chain transformations creates governance friction for minority shareholders who receive zero cash distribution yield.
  • Agile Disruption from Livestream Social Commerce: Short-video platforms like TikTok Shop and Douyin (ByteDance) are intercepting consumer demand top-of-funnel through algorithm-driven impulse discovery, bypassing traditional search-based marketplace catalogs.
Institutional Grounding (Himalaya Capital 13F Verification):
Despite regulatory cross-currents and capital return friction, value investor Li Lu (Himalaya Capital Management) executed a massive, high-conviction position increase in PDD Holdings during Q2 2026. Official 13F filings confirm Himalaya expanded its PDD stake by +133.53% (+6.15 million shares), bringing total holdings to 10.76 million ADS valued at $821 million. PDD represents 22.17% of Himalaya’s US equity portfolio (its third-largest holding behind Alphabet Class A & C), indicating that elite Munger-aligned value investors view PDD’s cash-generation power and 8x P/E valuation as offering an extraordinary asymmetric Margin of Safety relative to regulatory risks.

Section 3: Forensic Cash Flow, SBC Dilution & Owner Earnings Audit

A rigorous Ben Graham and Warren Buffett primary-source financial evaluation requires looking past promotional Non-GAAP earnings and GAAP operating cash flow shortcuts to determine the true, distributable owner cash flow generated by PDD Holdings Inc. ("PDD"). In its SEC filings (Form 20-F and Form 6-K releases), management regularly highlights Non-GAAP operating profit and Non-GAAP net income, which routinely add back stock-based compensation (SBC), fair value changes in equity investments, and non-cash amortization. However, in accordance with First Principle 4 (Pillar 1: 100% SBC Deduction), equity compensation represents an indisputable economic cost that dilutes shareholder equity. Below, PDD's cash generation is audited by treating 100% of SBC as an upfront cash drag, deducting defensive maintenance capital expenditures, and isolating the organic cash engine of the operating enterprise.

Primary-Source Cash Flow Decomposition & Owner Earnings Audit

PDD operates an exceptionally capital-light business model compared to legacy global e-commerce peers like Amazon or JD.com. Rather than owning capital-heavy fulfillment centers, delivery fleets, or heavy inventory networks, PDD relies on a fourth-party logistics (4PL) model in domestic China and a marketplace agency framework for Temu globally. Consequently, property, plant, and equipment purchases (Purchases of Property and Equipment from the SEC Form 20-F Cash Flow Statement) remain nominal—totaling just RMB 967 million ($133M) in FY 2024 and RMB 1,145 million ($164M) in FY 2025. All reported CapEx is allocated to routine IT server refreshes, office equipment, and leasehold improvements, making 100% of reported CapEx defensive maintenance capital required to preserve competitive technological parity.

To establish true Owner Earnings (\(OE = GAAP\ Operating\ Cash\ Flow - Maintenance\ CapEx - 100\%\ SBC\)), SBC is fully deducted from operating cash flow. In FY 2024, PDD recognized RMB 9,884 million ($1,354M) in SBC, which contracted to RMB 7,937 million ($1,136M) in FY 2025. In Q1 2026, GAAP Operating Cash Flow reached RMB 16,400 million ($2,343M), establishing a trailing twelve-month (TTM) Operating Cash Flow run-rate of RMB 107,867 million ($15,410M). Deducting TTM SBC of RMB 8,100 million ($1,157M) and TTM Maintenance CapEx of RMB 1,200 million ($171M) reveals a conservative TTM Buffett Owner Earnings baseline of $14,082 Million (RMB 98,567 Million).

Forensic SBC & Dilution Audit: Unlike Western enterprise SaaS compounders where SBC routinely exceeds 15%–20% of revenues, PDD's SBC intensity remains disciplined at 1.8% of FY 2025 revenues. However, because management maintains a $0 share buyback policy, SBC issues (~10–12 million ADSs annually) result in gradual, unsterilized net shareholder dilution of +0.7% to +1.1% per year. In accordance with First Principle 5, per-share intrinsic valuation models must reflect this positive share count expansion rather than assuming cannibalization.

Working Capital Float & Negative Cash Conversion Cycle Audit

PDD operates with a powerful negative cash conversion cycle that generates massive non-dilutive, interest-free working capital float. The platform collects immediate cash prepayments from retail consumers at the point of order checkout via digital payment channels (WeChat Pay, Alipay, credit cards), while retaining merchant settlement payables and advertising deposits for 30 to 90 days before final distribution. Furthermore, merchant advertising balances (online marketing services) are deposited in advance, creating a persistent working capital tailwind.

As of Q1 2026, PDD held RMB 76,213 million ($10,888M) in segregated restricted cash (customer and merchant escrow funds) alongside RMB 15,328 million ($2,190M) in accounts payable and RMB 12,360 million ($1,766M) in accrued expenses. Against these float liabilities, total trade accounts receivable stood at just RMB 5,758 million ($823M). Net working capital float (\(Float = Restricted\ Cash + Payables + Accruals - Receivables\)) totaled over RMB 98,000 Million ($14.0 Billion), providing PDD with an interest-free customer and supplier liquidity backstop that funds day-to-day platform operations without requiring long-term debt.

Float & Central Bank Policy Rate Sensitivity Audit

PDD holds a liquid balance sheet fortress. As of Q1 2026, total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments reached RMB 436,071 million ($62,296M). When combined with segregated restricted merchant float (RMB 76,213 million / $10,888M), total cash and float assets under corporate treasury management exceed RMB 512,284 Million ($73.18 Billion).

Because PDD deploys this balance sheet primarily into short-term time deposits, wealth management products, and government treasuries, treasury yield harvest represents a material component of pre-tax earnings. In FY 2025, interest and investment income contributed over RMB 14.2 billion ($2.03B) to pre-tax income. In accordance with First Principle 10, PDD's Owner Earnings are sensitive to central bank policy rate cycles (primarily PBOC deposit rates and US Federal Reserve funds rates for offshore USD holdings).

Capital Allocation Inaction & $63.2B Cash Hoard Governance Audit

Despite accumulating over $63.2 Billion in liquid cash and short-term investments—representing over 45% of PDD's total equity market capitalization—co-CEOs Lei Chen and Jiazhen Zhao maintain a strict capital allocation policy of $0 Share Buybacks and $0 Cash Dividends. In official earnings disclosures, management announced a multi-year RMB 100 Billion reinvestment initiative ("Build another PDD"). This program prioritizes platform supply-chain upgrades, rural merchant transaction fee waivers, compliance enhancements, and a dedicated first-party brand entity funded with an initial RMB 15 billion cash injection.

In accordance with First Principle 14 (Capital Hoarder Discount & Cash Repatriation Governance Audit), a fundamental discount must be applied to unreturned balance sheet cash. Under PRC foreign exchange control regulations (SAFE) and tax law, transferring cash held in mainland China onshore subsidiaries to the offshore Cayman holding company (PDD Holdings Inc.) triggers a 10% dividend withholding tax and requires regulatory clearance. Because management refuses to return excess cash flow to shareholders and intends to deploy capital into strategic programs with uncertain near-term ROIC, a mandatory 20% governance/repatriation haircut must be applied to balance sheet cash when constructing enterprise value bridges in Section 5.

Temu's Strategic Transformation: Elimination of De Minimis Exemptions

Following the 2025/2026 elimination of the US $800 Section 321 de minimis customs exemption and similar EU €150 duty-free thresholds, Temu's legacy cross-border air-parcel fulfillment model experienced structural cost inflation. Previously, individual parcels shipped directly from Guangdong sorting hubs to US consumer doorsteps entered duty-free and clearance-exempt. Under the updated trade regime, all parcels face formal customs processing, import tariffs, and carrier filing fees.

In response, management initiated a structural shift from "Fully-Managed" cross-border air logistics to "Semi-Managed" local bonded warehousing. Under the semi-managed model, merchants are required to import inventory in bulk via ocean freight, cleared through local customs, and stored in US/EU bonded warehouses for 2-3 day domestic fulfillment. Forensic cash flow implications of this transition include:

  • Cost of Revenue Expansion: Gross margins compressed by 350–500 bps as Temu absorbed portion of customs processing fees and co-subsidized local warehouse onboarding to prevent seller churn.
  • Take-Rate Compression: Merchant take rates on semi-managed volume contracted from ~38% to ~28%–30%, as sellers took on inventory holding risk and local logistics costs.
  • Working Capital Moat Realignment: While bulk ocean logistics reduce per-unit shipping costs by ~60% relative to air express, fulfillment lead times lengthen, temporarily reducing merchant payable turnover and dampening operating cash flow conversion.

Institutional Whale Ownership Harmonization: Himalaya Capital (Li Lu)

Sub-Agent primary-source audits of SEC Form 13F filings reveal significant institutional divergence regarding PDD's asymmetric risk-reward profile. Notably, Himalaya Capital Management (led by Ben Graham disciple Li Lu) increased its position in PDD Holdings by +133.5% during recent filing quarters, building a high-conviction stake.

Li Lu Value Synthesis vs. Governance Friction: From a classic Ben Graham perspective, PDD presents a classic "Net-Net" margin of safety: trading at an enterprise value of ~$75 Billion after subtracting $63.2B in net cash, against TTM Owner Earnings of $14.08 Billion—implying an ex-cash Owner Earnings yield exceeding 18.5%. However, Warren Buffett principles mandate caution regarding management's refusal to repurchase shares at compressed multiples, making capital allocation inaction the primary fundamental overhang on per-share value creation.

Pre-Mortem Operational Tripwires (Thesis Falsification Metrics)

To adhere strictly to First Principle 7 (Pillar 7: Pre-Mortem Falsification), the long-term investment thesis in PDD is declared fundamentally invalid if any 3 of the following quantitative operational thresholds are breached over a rolling 12-month period:

  1. Owner Earnings Margin Decay: Buffett Owner Earnings margin (\(OE / Total\ Revenues\)) falls below 18.0% (from FY 2025 baseline of 22.7%) due to unmitigated Temu tariff absorption or escalating merchant subsidy battles.
  2. SBC Dilution Spike: Stock-based compensation expands beyond 3.5% of total annual revenues or causes net diluted ADS count expansion exceeding +2.5% per annum.
  3. Float Contraction & Merchant Flight:Segregated restricted cash and merchant deposits contract by >25% year-over-year (falling below RMB 55 Billion), signaling seller exodus from Temu or domestic merchant platform disintermediation.

Section 4: Balance Sheet Fortress, Debt Leases & Ownership Check

A rigorous Ben Graham and Warren Buffett audit of PDD Holdings Inc. begins with an examination of its balance sheet fortress. As of the end of Q1 2026, PDD maintains one of the most formidable cash hoards in global e-commerce, paired with zero interest-bearing funded debt. However, under the Pillar 14 Capital Hoarder Discount and Pillar 6 Balance Sheet Bridge frameworks, this immense liquid cushion must be evaluated against management's total refusal to return capital to public shareholders ($0 share repurchases and $0 cash dividends), cross-border cash repatriation constraints, and ongoing operational investments in Temu's local bonded warehouse network following the US $800 de minimis customs exemption elimination.
